### omarchy/bin/omarchy-tailscale-receive
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Save incoming Taildrop files and announce them
# omarchy:args=[--once] [directory]
# omarchy:examples=omarchy tailscale receive | omarchy tailscale receive --once ~/Desktop

set -euo pipefail

once=false
if [[ ${1:-} == "--once" ]]; then
  once=true
  shift
fi

dir="${1:-${XDG_DOWNLOAD_DIR:-$HOME/Downloads}}"

# Taildrop lands in a staging directory next door rather than straight in the
# downloads directory: waiting for a delivery can take hours, and everything
# else that shows up meanwhile is somebody else's file. Same filesystem, so
# handing the finished file over is a rename.
staging="$dir/.omarchy-taildrop"
mkdir -p "$staging"

# Take the name by linking to it rather than by looking and then renaming.
# link(2) refuses an existing name, so nothing can land on the chosen one in
# the gap between the two. Staging shares the filesystem with the downloads
# directory, so the link always resolves and unlinking the staged name
# finishes the move. Prints the name it took.
claim_path() {
  local staged="$1" name="${staged##*/}" base ext candidate index=0

  base="${name%.*}"
  ext="${name#"$base"}"
  [[ -z $base ]] && { base="$name"; ext=""; }

  while (( index < 1000 )); do
    if (( index == 0 )); then
      candidate="$dir/$name"
    else
      candidate="$dir/$base-$index$ext"
    fi

    if ln -- "$staged" "$candidate" 2>/dev/null; then
      rm -f -- "$staged"
      printf '%s\n' "$candidate"
      return 0
    fi

    # Only a taken name is worth another spin. Anything else failed the link
    # itself, and the file keeps its place in staging for the next run.
    [[ -e $candidate ]] || return 1

    ((index++))
  done

  return 1
}

announce() {
  local path="$1"
  local name="${path##*/}"
  # Untrusted received files should not be decoded automatically for a preview.
  local args=("$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.received "$name")" "$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.savedTo "${dir/#$HOME/~}")" -u critical -g 󰒊)

  # Announcing is best-effort: the file is already delivered, and under `set -e`
  # a notification outage would otherwise kill the long-running receiver.
  omarchy-notification-send "${args[@]}" --exec xdg-open "$path" || true
}

deliver() {
  local staged target

  while IFS= read -r staged; do
    target=$(claim_path "$staged") || continue
    announce "$target"
  done < <(find "$staging" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1)
}

# Anything left staged by an interrupted run still deserves delivering.
deliver

while true; do
  if ! tailscale file get --wait --conflict=rename "$staging"; then
    $once && exit 1
    sleep 10
    continue
  fi

  deliver
  $once && exit 0
done

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-tailscale-send
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Send files to a machine on your tailnet with Taildrop
# omarchy:args=<machine> [file...]
# omarchy:examples=omarchy tailscale send dhh-fd | omarchy tailscale send dhh-fd ~/Downloads/notes.pdf

set -euo pipefail

if (($# < 1)); then
  echo "Usage: omarchy-tailscale-send <machine> [file...]" >&2
  exit 1
fi

machine="$1"
shift

# Address the machine by whatever name we were handed, but talk about it by
# its short name, so a MagicDNS name does not spill into every message.
name="${machine%%.*}"

files=("$@")

if ((${#files[@]} == 0)); then
  # Command substitution so the chooser's exit status survives: reading it
  # through a process substitution reports success for a chooser that never
  # opened, which is indistinguishable here from someone deciding not to send.
  picked=$(omarchy-file-select --title "$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.sendToTitle "$name")" --multiple) || status=$?

  if ((${status:-0} > 1)); then
    omarchy-notification-send -g "󰒊" -u critical "$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.sendFailed "$name")" \
      "$(omarchy-i18n share.chooserClosed)"
    exit 1
  fi

  readarray -t files <<<"$picked"
  [[ -n $picked ]] || exit 0
fi

if ((${#files[@]} == 1)); then
  what=$(basename "${files[0]}")
else
  what=$(omarchy-i18n --count "${#files[@]}" tailscale.fileCount "${#files[@]}")
fi

if error=$(tailscale file cp --update-interval=0 -- "${files[@]}" "$machine:" 2>&1); then
  omarchy-notification-send -g "󰒊" "$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.sent "$name")" "$what"
else
  omarchy-notification-send -g "󰒊" -u critical "$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.sendFailed "$name")" "${error:-$(omarchy-i18n tailscale.transferFailed)}"
  exit 1
fi

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-bg-boot-intro
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Play the current background's matching theme intro
# omarchy:hidden=true

set -euo pipefail

state_home="$HOME/.local/state"
current_dir="$state_home/omarchy/current"
current_background_link="$current_dir/background"
marker="$state_home/omarchy/background-intro.session-id"
toggle="$state_home/omarchy/toggles/background-intros-off"
video_extensions=(mp4 m4v mov webm mkv avi)

resolve_intro() {
  local background
  local stem
  local extension
  local intro

  background=$(readlink -f "${1:-$current_background_link}" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
  [[ -f $background ]] || return 1
  case ${background,,} in
  *.jpg | *.jpeg | *.png | *.bmp | *.webp) ;;
  *) return 1 ;;
  esac

  stem=${background##*/}
  stem=${stem%.*}
  for extension in "${video_extensions[@]}"; do
    intro="${background%/*}/intros/$stem.$extension"
    if [[ -f $intro ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$intro"
      return 0
    fi
  done
  return 1
}

# Preparation is speculative: the selected staged clip is compared again by OWE.
prepare_theme_intro() {
  local theme="$1" background remembered name source intro
  local -a names=()
  [[ -n $theme && $theme != .* && $theme != */* ]] || return 0
  [[ ! -f $toggle ]] && ! animations_off || return 0
  owe warm >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
  [[ $(cat "$current_dir/theme.name" 2>/dev/null) != "$theme" ]] || return 0
  remembered=$(cat "$state_home/omarchy/theme-backgrounds/$theme" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ ${remembered%/*} == "$current_dir/theme/backgrounds" ]]; then
    name=${remembered##*/}
  elif [[ -f $remembered ]]; then
    background="$remembered"
  else
    mapfile -d '' -t names < <(
      find -L "$HOME/.config/omarchy/backgrounds/$theme" -maxdepth 1 -type f -print0 2>/dev/null | sort -z
    )
    if (( ${#names[@]} > 0 )); then
      background=${names[0]}
    else
      mapfile -d '' -t names < <(
        find -L "$OMARCHY_PATH/themes/$theme/backgrounds" "$HOME/.config/omarchy/themes/$theme/backgrounds" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
          \( -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.jpeg' -o -iname '*.png' -o -iname '*.bmp' -o -iname '*.webp' \) -printf '%f\0' 2>/dev/null | sort -zu
      )
      (( ${#names[@]} > 0 )) || return 0
      name=${names[0]}
    fi
  fi
  if [[ -n ${name:-} ]]; then
    for source in "$HOME/.config/omarchy/themes/$theme" "$OMARCHY_PATH/themes/$theme"; do
      if [[ -f $source/backgrounds/$name ]]; then
        background="$source/backgrounds/$name"
        break
      fi
    done
  fi
  [[ -n ${background:-} ]] || return 0
  intro=$(resolve_intro "$background" || true)
  [[ -z $intro ]] || owe intro-prepare "$intro" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

animations_off() {
  [[ $(hyprctl -j getoption animations:enabled 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.bool' 2>/dev/null) == "false" ]]
}

theme_switch=false
intro_prepared=false
expected_background=""
expected_theme=""
case ${1:-} in
  "") ;;
  --prepare-theme)
    prepare_theme_intro "${2:-}"
    exit 0
    ;;
  --resolve-only)
    resolve_intro "${2:-}" || true
    exit 0
    ;;
  --resolve-startup)
    if [[ ! -f $toggle ]] && ! animations_off; then
      resolve_intro || true
    fi
    exit 0
    ;;
  --theme-switch)
    theme_switch=true
    expected_background=$(readlink -f "${2:-}" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1
    expected_theme=${3:-}
    intro_prepared=${4:-false}
    [[ -n $expected_theme ]] || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-bg-boot-intro [--resolve-only [background]|--resolve-startup|--prepare-theme theme|--theme-switch background theme-id [prepared]]" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

if [[ $theme_switch == false ]]; then
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$marker")"
  exec 9>"$state_home/omarchy/background-intro.lock"
  flock 9

  session_id=${OMARCHY_SESSION_ID:-${HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE:-}}
  [[ -n $session_id ]] || exit 0
  if [[ -f $marker && $(<"$marker") == "$session_id" ]]; then
    exit 0
  fi

  marker_staged=$(mktemp "$state_home/omarchy/.background-intro.session-id.XXXXXX")
  trap 'rm -f "$marker_staged"' EXIT
  printf '%s\n' "$session_id" >"$marker_staged"
  mv -f "$marker_staged" "$marker"
  trap - EXIT
  exec 9>&-
fi

selection_current() {
  [[ $(readlink -f "$current_background_link") == "$expected_background" &&
    $(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$current_dir/theme" 2>/dev/null) == "$expected_theme" ]]
}

if [[ $theme_switch == true ]] && ! selection_current; then
  exit 0
fi

if [[ -f $toggle ]] || animations_off; then
  [[ $theme_switch == false ]] || exit 1
  exit 0
fi

intro=$(resolve_intro || true)
if [[ -z $intro ]]; then
  [[ $theme_switch == false ]] || exit 1
  exit 0
fi

if [[ $theme_switch == true && $intro_prepared != "true" ]]; then
  owe refresh >/dev/null || exit 1
elif [[ $theme_switch == false ]]; then
  deadline=$((SECONDS + 5))
  while ! timeout 1 owe status >/dev/null 2>&1; do
    if (( SECONDS >= deadline )); then
      exit 0
    fi
    sleep 0.2
  done
  (( SECONDS < deadline )) || exit 0
fi

# The asynchronous outgoing cover must reach the compositor before playback
# can hide the shell background. Older shells have no readiness method.
if [[ $theme_switch == true ]]; then
  deadline=$((SECONDS + 3))
  while true; do
    cover_status=$(omarchy-shell shell themeIntroCoverStatus "$expected_theme" 2>/dev/null || true)
    case $cover_status in
      loading)
        (( SECONDS < deadline )) || exit 1
        sleep 0.01
        ;;
      error) exit 1 ;;
      superseded) exit 0 ;;
      *) break ;;
    esac
  done
fi

if [[ $theme_switch == true ]] && ! selection_current; then
  exit 0
fi

# A selection or setting changed while OWE was starting no longer permits this intro.
if [[ ! -f $toggle && $intro == "$(resolve_intro || true)" ]] && ! animations_off; then
  if [[ $theme_switch == true && $intro_prepared == "true" ]]; then
    owe intro --start first-frame --refresh "$intro"
  else
    owe intro --start first-frame "$intro"
  fi
elif [[ $theme_switch == true ]]; then
  exit 1
fi

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-bg-intro
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:args=<enable|disable|toggle|status>
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme bg intro toggle | omarchy theme bg intro disable

set -euo pipefail

toggle="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/background-intros-off"
case ${1:-} in
  enable)
    rm -f "$toggle"
    omarchy-notification-send "$(omarchy-i18n theme.backgroundIntros)" "$(omarchy-i18n common.enabled)"

    else
      omarchy-theme-bg-intro disable
    fi
    ;;
  status)
    [[ ! -f $toggle ]]
    ;;
  *)
    echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-bg-intro <enable|disable|toggle|status>" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-bg-next
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Cycle to the next background for the current theme
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme bg next

THEME_NAME=$(cat "$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.name" 2>/dev/null)
THEME_BACKGROUNDS_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/backgrounds/"
USER_BACKGROUNDS_PATH="$HOME/.config/omarchy/backgrounds/$THEME_NAME/"
CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/background"

mapfile -d '' -t BACKGROUNDS < <(
  find -L "$USER_BACKGROUNDS_PATH" "$THEME_BACKGROUNDS_PATH" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
    \( -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.jpeg' -o -iname '*.png' -o -iname '*.gif' -o -iname '*.bmp' -o -iname '*.webp' \
       -o -iname '*.mp4' -o -iname '*.m4v' -o -iname '*.mov' -o -iname '*.webm' -o -iname '*.mkv' -o -iname '*.avi' \) \
    -print0 2>/dev/null | sort -z
)
TOTAL=${#BACKGROUNDS[@]}

if (( TOTAL == 0 )); then
  omarchy-notification-send "$(omarchy-i18n theme.noBackground)" -t 2000
else
  # Get current background from symlink
  if [[ -L $CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK ]]; then
    CURRENT_BACKGROUND=$(readlink "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK")
  else
    # Default to first background if no symlink exists
    CURRENT_BACKGROUND=""
  fi

  # Find current background index
  INDEX=-1
  for i in "${!BACKGROUNDS[@]}"; do
    if [[ ${BACKGROUNDS[$i]} == "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND" ]]; then
      INDEX=$i
      break
    fi
  done

  # Get next background (wrap around)
  if (( INDEX == -1 )); then
    # Use the first background when no match was found
    NEW_BACKGROUND="${BACKGROUNDS[0]}"
  else
    NEXT_INDEX=$(((INDEX + 1) % TOTAL))
    NEW_BACKGROUND="${BACKGROUNDS[$NEXT_INDEX]}"
  fi

  omarchy-theme-bg-set "$NEW_BACKGROUND"
fi

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-bg-set
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Set the current background image or video
# omarchy:args=<path-to-media>
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme bg set ~/Pictures/background.png

if [[ -z $1 ]]; then
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-bg-set <path-to-media>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

BACKGROUND="$(realpath "$1")"
CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/background"

if [[ ! -f $BACKGROUND ]]; then
  echo "File does not exist: $BACKGROUND" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Create symlink to the new background media
ln -nsf "$BACKGROUND" "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK"

# Update the live shell background when it is running. Nothing watches the
# symlink, so this is how the shell learns of the new background.
omarchy-shell -q background set "$BACKGROUND"

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-color
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Resolve semantic colors from an Omarchy theme colors.toml
# omarchy:args=[--file <colors.toml>] (--all | --raw | <key> [fallback])
# omarchy:hidden=true

# Shared colors.toml parser/resolver. The alias/fallback cascade mirrors what
# omarchy-theme-set-templates bakes into the generated configs at theme-set
# time, so every consumer (templates, OSC sequences, tmux, GNOME, previews)
# resolves the exact same palette.
#
#   --all            print every resolved key<TAB>value pair (sorted by key)
#   --raw            print only the key<TAB>value pairs defined in the file
#   <key> [fallback] print one resolved value; the fallback is tried as
#                    another palette key first, then used verbatim
#
# Theme mode precedence: `mode` key, legacy `theme_type` key, a light.mode
# file beside the colors.toml, background luminance auto-detect, dark.

COLORS_FILE="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml"
OUTPUT=""
QUERY_KEY=""
QUERY_FALLBACK=""

usage() {
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-color [--file <colors.toml>] (--all | --raw | <key> [fallback])"
}

while (( $# > 0 )); do
  case "$1" in
    --file)
      COLORS_FILE="${2:-}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --all)
      OUTPUT="all"
      shift
      ;;
    --raw)
      OUTPUT="raw"
      shift
      ;;
    -h | --help)
      usage
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      if [[ -z $QUERY_KEY ]]; then
        QUERY_KEY="$1"
      elif [[ -z $QUERY_FALLBACK ]]; then
        QUERY_FALLBACK="$1"
      else
        usage >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ -z $OUTPUT && -z $QUERY_KEY ]] || [[ -n $OUTPUT && -n $QUERY_KEY ]]; then
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

COLORS_DIR=$(dirname "$COLORS_FILE")

declare -A THEME_COLORS

# Mix two hex colors. Amount may be a fraction (0.30) or percentage (30%).
mix_color() {
  local start="${1#\#}"
  local end="${2#\#}"
  local amount="$3"

  awk -v start="$start" -v end="$end" -v amount="$amount" '
    function hex_value(char) {
      return index("0123456789abcdef", tolower(char)) - 1
    }

    function hex_pair_to_int(hex, idx) {
      return hex_value(substr(hex, idx, 1)) * 16 + hex_value(substr(hex, idx + 1, 1))
    }

    BEGIN {
      if (amount ~ /%$/) {
        sub(/%$/, "", amount)
        amount = amount / 100
      } else {
        amount += 0
        if (amount > 1) amount = amount / 100
      }

      if (amount < 0) amount = 0
      if (amount > 1) amount = 1

      start_r = hex_pair_to_int(start, 1)
      start_g = hex_pair_to_int(start, 3)
      start_b = hex_pair_to_int(start, 5)
      end_r = hex_pair_to_int(end, 1)
      end_g = hex_pair_to_int(end, 3)
      end_b = hex_pair_to_int(end, 5)

      red = int(start_r * (1 - amount) + end_r * amount + 0.5)
      green = int(start_g * (1 - amount) + end_g * amount + 0.5)
      blue = int(start_b * (1 - amount) + end_b * amount + 0.5)

      printf "#%02x%02x%02x\n", red, green, blue
    }
  '
}

alias_theme_color() {
  local key="$1"
  local fallback="$2"

  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[$key]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[$key]="${THEME_COLORS[$fallback]}"
}

resolve_theme_mode() {
  local bg_hex lum

  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[mode]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[mode]="${THEME_COLORS[theme_type]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[mode]} ]] && return

  if [[ -f $COLORS_DIR/light.mode ]]; then
    THEME_COLORS[mode]="light"
  elif [[ ${THEME_COLORS[background]} =~ ^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$ ]]; then
    bg_hex="${THEME_COLORS[background]#\#}"
    lum=$(( $(printf "%d" "0x${bg_hex:0:2}") + $(printf "%d" "0x${bg_hex:2:2}") + $(printf "%d" "0x${bg_hex:4:2}") ))
    (( lum > 382 )) && THEME_COLORS[mode]="light" || THEME_COLORS[mode]="dark"
  else
    THEME_COLORS[mode]="dark"
  fi
}

parse_colors_file() {
  local key value

  [[ -f $COLORS_FILE ]] || return 0

  while IFS='=' read -r key value; do
    key="${key//[\"\' ]/}"                # strip quotes and spaces from key
    [[ $key && $key != \#* ]] || continue # skip empty lines and comments

    if [[ $value == *[\"\']* ]]; then
      value="${value#*[\"\']}"
      value="${value%%[\"\']*}" # extract value between quotes (ignores inline comments)
    else
      value="${value#"${value%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
      value="${value%"${value##*[![:space:]]}"}" # trim unquoted values
    fi

    # Values reach consumers as sed replacement text, so the charset excludes
    # the delimiter, backslash, and & while still covering everything a real
    # palette holds: hex, rgb()/rgba() lists, gradient angles like -45deg,
    # decimals, and bare words. Rejections are announced so a third-party theme
    # doesn't lose a key silently and leave a raw {{ placeholder }} behind.
    if [[ ! $key =~ ^[abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789_-]+$ ]]; then
      printf 'omarchy-theme-color: skipping key with unsupported characters\n' >&2
      continue
    fi

    if [[ ! $value =~ ^[abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789#(),._+/%\ -]*$ ]]; then
      printf 'omarchy-theme-color: skipping %s: unsupported characters in value\n' "$key" >&2
      continue
    fi

    THEME_COLORS[$key]="$value"
    [[ $OUTPUT == "raw" ]] && printf '%s\t%s\n' "$key" "$value"
  done <"$COLORS_FILE"

  return 0
}

resolve_theme_colors() {
  local key

  # Accept the complete legacy short-name palette before applying ANSI
  # fallbacks or deriving shades. Canonical names take precedence when a theme
  # defines both forms.
  declare -A legacy_palette_alias=(
    [background]=bg
    [dark_background]=dark_bg
    [darker_background]=darker_bg
    [lighter_background]=lighter_bg
    [foreground]=fg
    [dark_foreground]=dark_fg
    [light_foreground]=light_fg
    [bright_foreground]=bright_fg
  )
  for key in "${!legacy_palette_alias[@]}"; do
    alias_theme_color "$key" "${legacy_palette_alias[$key]}"
  done

  # Themes generated before the semantic palette may only define ANSI names.
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[background]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[background]="${THEME_COLORS[color0]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[foreground]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[foreground]="${THEME_COLORS[color7]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[background]} ]] && THEME_COLORS[color0]="${THEME_COLORS[background]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[foreground]} ]] && THEME_COLORS[color7]="${THEME_COLORS[foreground]}"

  # Legacy compatibility: map ANSI color0..color15 to semantic names.
  declare -A legacy_alias=(
    [red]=color1
    [green]=color2
    [yellow]=color3
    [blue]=color4
    [magenta]=color5
    [cyan]=color6
    [bright_red]=color9
    [bright_green]=color10
    [bright_yellow]=color11
    [bright_blue]=color12
    [bright_magenta]=color13
    [bright_cyan]=color14
  )
  for key in "${!legacy_alias[@]}"; do
    alias_theme_color "$key" "${legacy_alias[$key]}"
  done
  alias_theme_color magenta purple
  alias_theme_color bright_magenta bright_purple

  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[light_foreground]} ]]  || THEME_COLORS[light_foreground]="${THEME_COLORS[color7]:-${THEME_COLORS[foreground]}}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_foreground]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[bright_foreground]="${THEME_COLORS[color15]:-${THEME_COLORS[foreground]}}"
  THEME_COLORS[cursor]="${THEME_COLORS[bright_foreground]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[lighter_background]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[lighter_background]="${THEME_COLORS[color0]:-${THEME_COLORS[background]}}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[dark_foreground]} ]]    || THEME_COLORS[dark_foreground]="${THEME_COLORS[color8]:-${THEME_COLORS[foreground]}}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[muted]} ]]      || THEME_COLORS[muted]="${THEME_COLORS[color8]:-${THEME_COLORS[dark_foreground]}}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[selection]} ]]            || THEME_COLORS[selection]="${THEME_COLORS[selection_background]:-${THEME_COLORS[color8]:-${THEME_COLORS[color0]:-${THEME_COLORS[background]}}}}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[selection_background]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[selection_background]="${THEME_COLORS[selection]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[selection_foreground]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[selection_foreground]="${THEME_COLORS[bright_foreground]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[orange]} ]]               || THEME_COLORS[orange]="${THEME_COLORS[yellow]}"
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[brown]} ]]      || THEME_COLORS[brown]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[orange]}" "#000000" 50%)

  # Auto-derive shades from base accents when not defined and not aliased from colorN
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[dark_background]} ]]   || THEME_COLORS[dark_background]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[background]}" "#000000" 25%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[darker_background]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[darker_background]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[background]}" "#000000" 50%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_red]} ]]    || THEME_COLORS[bright_red]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[red]}" "#ffffff" 20%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_yellow]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[bright_yellow]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[yellow]}" "#ffffff" 20%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_green]} ]]  || THEME_COLORS[bright_green]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[green]}" "#ffffff" 20%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_cyan]} ]]   || THEME_COLORS[bright_cyan]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[cyan]}" "#ffffff" 20%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_blue]} ]]   || THEME_COLORS[bright_blue]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[blue]}" "#ffffff" 20%)
  [[ ${THEME_COLORS[bright_magenta]} ]] || THEME_COLORS[bright_magenta]=$(mix_color "${THEME_COLORS[magenta]}" "#ffffff" 20%)
  alias_theme_color purple magenta
  alias_theme_color bright_purple bright_magenta

  # Keep semantic themes compatible with consumers that still reference the
  # legacy ANSI names directly.
  declare -A ansi_alias=(
    [color0]=background
    [color1]=red
    [color2]=green
    [color3]=yellow
    [color4]=blue
    [color5]=magenta
    [color6]=cyan
    [color7]=foreground
    [color8]=muted
    [color9]=bright_red
    [color10]=bright_green
    [color11]=bright_yellow
    [color12]=bright_blue
    [color13]=bright_magenta
    [color14]=bright_cyan
    [color15]=bright_foreground
  )
  for key in "${!ansi_alias[@]}"; do
    alias_theme_color "$key" "${ansi_alias[$key]}"
  done

  # Keep canonical themes compatible with old user templates and consumers
  # that still query the short palette names directly.
  for key in "${!legacy_palette_alias[@]}"; do
    if [[ ${THEME_COLORS[$key]} ]]; then
      THEME_COLORS["${legacy_palette_alias[$key]}"]="${THEME_COLORS[$key]}"
    fi
  done

  resolve_theme_mode
  THEME_COLORS[theme_type]="${THEME_COLORS[mode]}"
}

parse_colors_file

if [[ $OUTPUT == "raw" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

resolve_theme_colors

if [[ $OUTPUT == "all" ]]; then
  while IFS= read -r key; do
    printf '%s\t%s\n' "$key" "${THEME_COLORS[$key]}"
  done < <(printf '%s\n' "${!THEME_COLORS[@]}" | LC_ALL=C sort)
  exit 0
fi

value="${THEME_COLORS[$QUERY_KEY]:-}"
if [[ -z $value && -n $QUERY_FALLBACK ]]; then
  value="${THEME_COLORS[$QUERY_FALLBACK]:-$QUERY_FALLBACK}"
fi

[[ -n $value ]] || exit 1
printf '%s\n' "$value"

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-colors-from-alacritty
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Generate a theme's colors.toml from its alacritty.toml palette
# omarchy:args=<theme-dir>
# omarchy:hidden=true

set -e

THEME_SOURCE="${1:-}"
COLORS_OUTPUT="$THEME_SOURCE/colors.toml"
ALACRITTY_FILE="$THEME_SOURCE/alacritty.toml"

if [[ -z $THEME_SOURCE ]]; then
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-colors-from-alacritty <theme-dir>" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# Skip if colors.toml already exists in source theme
if [[ -f $COLORS_OUTPUT ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Skip if no alacritty.toml to extract from
if [[ ! -f $ALACRITTY_FILE ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

# Parse the alacritty TOML in a single awk pass, emitting one
# "<dotted-path>\t#<hex>" pair per color-valued key. Dotted keys are
# normalized (`normal.black = ...` under [colors] becomes
# colors.normal.black, same as `black = ...` under [colors.normal]),
# with the section form taking precedence and the first valid
# occurrence of a key winning.
declare -A COLORS

while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value; do
  COLORS[$key]=$value
done < <(awk '
  /^[ \t]*\[/ {
    line = $0
    sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line)
    if (line ~ /^\[[^]]*\][ \t]*$/) {
      section = substr(line, 2, index(line, "]") - 2)
    } else {
      section = ""
    }
    next
  }

  section != "" {
    split_pos = index($0, "=")
    if (split_pos == 0) {
      next
    }

    key = substr($0, 1, split_pos - 1)
    gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", key)
    if (key == "" || key ~ /^#/) {
      next
    }

    value = substr($0, split_pos + 1)
    gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", value)

    # Accept a lone hex color, optionally 0x- or #-prefixed and quoted,
    # ignoring any trailing comment. The color always yields the first
    # run of six hex digits.
    if (value !~ /^["'\''](0[xX]|#)?[0-9a-fA-F]{6}(["'\'']([ \t]*#.*)?)?$/ &&
        value !~ /^(0[xX])?[0-9a-fA-F]{6}([ \t]*#.*)?$/) {
      next
    }
    match(value, /[0-9a-fA-F]{6}/)
    hex = tolower(substr(value, RSTART, RLENGTH))

    path = section "." key
    if (section == "colors" && index(key, ".") > 0) {
      if (!(path in dotted)) dotted[path] = hex
    } else {
      if (!(path in direct)) direct[path] = hex
    }
  }

  END {
    for (path in direct) print path "\t#" direct[path]
    for (path in dotted) if (!(path in direct)) print path "\t#" dotted[path]
  }
' "$ALACRITTY_FILE")

names=(black red green yellow blue magenta cyan white)

# Extract normal colors (color0-7)
for i in {0..7}; do
  name="${names[$i]}"
  printf -v "color$i" "%s" "${COLORS[colors.normal.$name]}"
done

# Validate we have all normal colors (required)
for c in color0 color1 color2 color3 color4 color5 color6 color7; do
  if [[ -z ${!c} ]]; then
    echo "Warning: Cannot extract all normal colors from $ALACRITTY_FILE, skipping generation" >&2
    exit 0
  fi
done

# Extract bright colors (color8-15), falling back to normal
for i in {0..7}; do
  normal="color$i"
  name="${names[$i]}"
  val="${COLORS[colors.bright.$name]}"
  printf -v "color$((i + 8))" "%s" "${val:-${!normal}}"
done

# Extract primary and selection colors
background="${COLORS[colors.primary.background]}"
foreground="${COLORS[colors.primary.foreground]}"
selection_background="${COLORS[colors.selection.background]}"

# Apply defaults
background=${background:-$color0}
foreground=${foreground:-$color7}
color0=$background
color7=$foreground
selection_background=${selection_background:-$foreground}
accent=$color4

mkdir -p "$THEME_SOURCE"

cat > "$COLORS_OUTPUT" <<EOF
accent = "$accent"
selection = "$selection_background"

background = "$background"
foreground = "$foreground"

color0 = "$color0"
color1 = "$color1"
color2 = "$color2"
color3 = "$color3"
color4 = "$color4"
color5 = "$color5"
color6 = "$color6"
color7 = "$color7"
color8 = "$color8"
color9 = "$color9"
color10 = "$color10"
color11 = "$color11"
color12 = "$color12"
color13 = "$color13"
color14 = "$color14"
color15 = "$color15"
EOF

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-dir
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Print the directory holding a theme, preferring a user-installed copy
# omarchy:args=<theme-name>
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme dir tokyo-night

theme="${1:-}"

if [[ -z $theme ]]; then
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-dir <theme-name>" >&2

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-extras
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=List the user-installed themes that came from a git clone
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme extras

# Exits nonzero when there are none, so a caller can ask whether any exist
# without reading the list. A symlinked theme is someone's working copy and a
# `.git` file is a worktree pointing elsewhere; neither is ours to pull.
status=1

for theme in ~/.config/omarchy/themes/*; do
  [[ ! -L $theme && -d $theme/.git ]] || continue
  echo "$theme"
  status=0
done

exit $status

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-install
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Install a theme from a git repository
# omarchy:args=[git-repo-url]
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme install https://github.com/example/omarchy-example-theme.git
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme install git@github.com:example/omarchy-example-theme.git

if [[ -z $1 ]]; then
  echo -e "\e[32mSee https://omarchy.org/themes/\n\e[0m"
  REPO_URL=$(gum input --placeholder="$(omarchy-i18n theme.repoPlaceholder)" --header="")
else
  REPO_URL="$1"
fi

if [[ -z $REPO_URL ]]; then
  exit 1
fi

# Refuse a URL that names a git option or a transport helper before cloning. The
# check is shared with omarchy-plugin-add and explains itself; a missing checker
# leaves this non-zero, which refuses the URL rather than cloning it.
omarchy-git-url-check "$REPO_URL" || exit 1

THEMES_DIR="$HOME/.config/omarchy/themes"

# Strip user@host: prefix from scp-style SSH URLs so basename sees just the path.
# git reads a URL as scp-style when a colon appears before any slash, so the path
# after it need not hold one: `git@host:omarchy-blue-theme.git` is a repo in that
# user's home, and leaving its prefix on names the theme after the whole URL.
REPO_PATH="$REPO_URL"
[[ $REPO_PATH != *"://"* && $REPO_PATH == *:* && ${REPO_PATH%%:*} != */* ]] && REPO_PATH="${REPO_PATH#*:}"
THEME_NAME=$(basename -- "$REPO_PATH" .git | sed -E 's/^omarchy-//; s/-theme$//' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
THEME_PATH="$THEMES_DIR/$THEME_NAME"

# The name comes from the URL, is joined into a path that is about to be
# removed, and then names a directory the rest of Omarchy passes around by
# name: Appearance > Unlock builds a command line out of the one the picker
# returned. So it is held to the characters a theme name needs rather than
# screened for the harm of the day -- a repo called `..` would take
# ~/.config/omarchy with it, and one called `a';'id` would carry its own
# command into that picker. The leading character is kept out of `.` and `-`,
# which also covers `host:-s/foo.git` leaving basename with `.git`.
# A bracket range follows the locale's collation, not ASCII: `[a-z]` takes in
# `é` under en_US.UTF-8. Pin the locale so the set is the one written here.
if ! (LC_ALL=C; [[ $THEME_NAME =~ ^[a-z0-9_][a-z0-9._+-]*$ ]]); then
  echo "Error: '$REPO_URL' does not give a usable theme name."
  exit 1
fi

# Remove existing theme if present
if [[ -d $THEME_PATH ]]; then
  rm -rf "$THEME_PATH"
fi

# Clone the repo directly to ~/.config/omarchy/themes
if ! git clone -- "$REPO_URL" "$THEME_PATH"; then
  echo "Error: Failed to clone theme repo."
  exit 1
fi

# Apply the new theme with omarchy-theme-set, which stages only the files an
# extra theme is allowed to contribute and names anything it dropped.
omarchy-theme-set "$THEME_NAME"

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-list
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=List available themes
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme list | omarchy theme set "Tokyo Night"

{
  find ~/.config/omarchy/themes/ -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 \( -type d -o -type l \) -printf '%f\n'
  find "$OMARCHY_PATH/themes/" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -printf '%f\n'
} | sort -u | sed -E 's/(^|-)([a-z])/\1\u\2/g; s/-/ /g'

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-osc
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Print OSC sequences for an Omarchy color theme
# omarchy:hidden=true

theme="${1:-$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml}"

[[ -f $theme ]] || exit 0

declare -A COLORS

while IFS=$'\t' read -r key value; do
  COLORS[$key]="$value"
done < <(omarchy-theme-color --file "$theme" --all)

emit_osc() {
  local code="$1"
  local key="$2"

  [[ -n ${COLORS[$key]:-} ]] || return 0
  printf '\033]%s;%s\007' "$code" "${COLORS[$key]}"
}

emit_osc 10 foreground
emit_osc 11 background
emit_osc 12 cursor
emit_osc 17 selection_background
emit_osc 19 selection_foreground

for i in {0..15}; do
  [[ -n ${COLORS[color$i]:-} ]] || continue
  printf '\033]4;%d;%s\007' "$i" "${COLORS[color$i]}"
done

# writes, so this waits for every retint rather than leaving some running.

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-remove
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Remove a user-installed theme
# omarchy:args=[theme-name]
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme remove "Tokyo Night"

if [[ -z $1 ]]; then
  mapfile -t extra_themes < <(find ~/.config/omarchy/themes -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -xtype l -printf '%f\n')

  if (( ${#extra_themes[@]} > 0 )); then
    mapfile -t extra_themes < <(printf '%s\n' "${extra_themes[@]}" | sort)
    THEME_NAME=$(omarchy-menu-select "$(omarchy-i18n theme.removeExtraTitle)" "${extra_themes[@]}" -- --width 520 --maxheight 520)
  else
    echo "No extra themes installed."
    exit 1
  fi
else
  THEME_NAME="$1"
fi

THEMES_DIR="$HOME/.config/omarchy/themes"
THEME_PATH="$THEMES_DIR/$THEME_NAME"

# Ensure a theme was set, and that the name cannot climb out of THEMES_DIR
# on its way into the rm below.
if [[ -z $THEME_NAME || $THEME_NAME == .* || $THEME_NAME == */* ]]; then
  exit 1
fi

# Check if theme exists before attempting removal
if [[ ! -d $THEME_PATH ]]; then
  echo "Error: Theme '$THEME_NAME' not found."
  exit 1
fi

# Now remove the theme directory for THEME_NAME
rm -rf "$THEME_PATH"
omarchy-notification-send "$(omarchy-i18n theme.removed)" "$THEME_NAME" || true
echo "Removed $THEME_NAME"

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Apply an Omarchy theme
# omarchy:args=<theme-name>
# omarchy:examples=omarchy theme list | omarchy theme set "Tokyo Night"

if [[ -z $1 ]]; then
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-set <theme-name>"
  exit 1
fi

CURRENT_THEME_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme"
CURRENT_THEME_NAME_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.name"
NEXT_THEME_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/next-theme"
CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/background"
THEME_BACKGROUND_STATE_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/theme-backgrounds"
BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_CACHE="$HOME/.cache/omarchy/background-transitions"
THEME_SET_LOCK="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-theme-set.lock"
THEME_SET_LOG="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/theme-set.log"
THEME_RETINT_LOCK="${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-theme-set-retint.lock"
THEME_GENERATION_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.generation"
USER_THEMES_PATH="$HOME/.config/omarchy/themes"
OMARCHY_THEMES_PATH="$OMARCHY_PATH/themes"

# What a theme installed from a git repo may not ship, because these run code.
# Hyprland requires a theme's hyprland.lua and gum_env.lua at login and Neovim
# loads its neovim.lua at startup, so no .lua from such a theme is staged at all.
# Each terminal config names the program the terminal launches, and vscode.json
# names an extension omarchy-theme-set-vscode installs, a VS Code extension being
# arbitrary JavaScript. Everything else a theme ships is colour and is kept.
#
# Adding a template for another terminal, or for another editor that loads Lua,
# means adding it here. test/shell.d/theme-staging-test.sh fails on a generated
# theme file that is neither denied here nor recorded there as colour-only.
INSTALLED_THEME_DENIED=(alacritty.toml foot.ini ghostty.conf kitty.conf vscode.json)
IGNORED_THEME_FILES=()

FAILED_THEME_COMMANDS=()

# Each command is an Omarchy command on the PATH this one already has, so it
# runs directly rather than through a login shell that rereads the profile.
# A background command would otherwise get /dev/null as stdin, and the browser
# policy asks for a sudo password on stdin when it is a terminal.
run_parallel() {
  local command index
  local -a commands=("$@") pids=()

  for command in "${commands[@]}"; do
    "$command" <&0 8>&- &
    pids+=("$!")
  done

  for index in "${!pids[@]}"; do
    wait "${pids[$index]}" || FAILED_THEME_COMMANDS+=("${commands[$index]}")
  done
}

# A retint that fails leaves one app on the old colours while the rest of the
# desktop moved on. The switch itself still succeeded, so this never changes
# the exit status. Name the command on stderr, and when that is the log a
# detached run writes, in a notification too, since nobody is watching it.
report_failed_theme_commands() {
  local detached="$1"

  (( ${#FAILED_THEME_COMMANDS[@]} > 0 )) || return 0

  echo "Theme retint failed: ${FAILED_THEME_COMMANDS[*]}" >&2
  if [[ $detached == "detached" ]]; then
    omarchy-notification-send -u normal "$(omarchy-i18n theme.notAppliedEverywhere)" \
      "$(omarchy-i18n theme.commandsFailed "${FAILED_THEME_COMMANDS[*]}" "$THEME_SET_LOG")" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  fi
}

shell_ipc() {
  timeout 2 omarchy-shell "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

wait_for_theme_intro() {
  local method="$1" token="$2" pending="$3" deadline=$((SECONDS + 3))
  while (( SECONDS < deadline )) && [[ $(omarchy-shell shell "$method" "$token" 2>/dev/null) == "$pending" ]]; do
    sleep 0.02
  done
}

is_video_path() {
  [[ ${1,,} =~ \.(mp4|m4v|mov|webm|mkv|avi)$ ]]
}

snapshot_background_path() {
  local background="$1"
  local name="$2"
  local snapshot extension

  [[ -f $background ]] || return
  is_video_path "$background" && return

  mkdir -p "$BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_CACHE"
  extension=${background##*.}
  snapshot="$BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_CACHE/$name-$$.$extension"
  ln "$background" "$snapshot" 2>/dev/null || cp "$background" "$snapshot"
  echo "$snapshot"
}

snapshot_current_background() {
  local current_background snapshot

  # An interrupted intro is still moving; its final still would flash as a
  # cover. Capture the frame already playing instead, when OWE supports it.
  mkdir -p "$BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_CACHE"
  snapshot="$BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_CACHE/previous-$$.ppm"
  if owe render "$(jq -nc --arg path "$snapshot" '{cmd: "snapshot", path: $path}')" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "$snapshot"
  else
    current_background=$(readlink -f "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK" 2>/dev/null || true)
    snapshot_background_path "$current_background" "previous"
  fi
}

theme_background_state_file() {
  local theme="$1"

  [[ -n $theme && ${theme##*/} == $theme && $theme != "." && $theme != ".." ]] || return 1
  printf '%s/%s\n' "$THEME_BACKGROUND_STATE_PATH" "$theme"
}

remember_current_theme_background() {
  local current_background state_file

  state_file=$(theme_background_state_file "$PREVIOUS_THEME_NAME") || return
  current_background=$(readlink -f "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK" 2>/dev/null || true)
  [[ -f $current_background ]] || return

  mkdir -p "$THEME_BACKGROUND_STATE_PATH"
  printf '%s\n' "$current_background" >"$state_file"
}

background_transition_uses_snapshots() {
  local next_background="$1"
  local current_background

  current_background=$(readlink -f "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK" 2>/dev/null || true)
  ! is_video_path "$current_background" && ! is_video_path "$next_background"
}

choose_theme_background() {
  local theme_path="${1:-$CURRENT_THEME_PATH}"
  local current_theme_backgrounds="$CURRENT_THEME_PATH/backgrounds"
  local backgrounds=()
  local current_background remembered_background state_file index next_index i

  CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND=""
  mapfile -d '' -t backgrounds < <(
    find -L "$HOME/.config/omarchy/backgrounds/$THEME_NAME/" "$theme_path/backgrounds/" -maxdepth 1 -type f \
      \( -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.jpeg' -o -iname '*.png' -o -iname '*.gif' -o -iname '*.bmp' -o -iname '*.webp' \
         -o -iname '*.mp4' -o -iname '*.m4v' -o -iname '*.mov' -o -iname '*.webm' -o -iname '*.mkv' -o -iname '*.avi' \) \
      -print0 2>/dev/null | sort -z
  )

  (( ${#backgrounds[@]} > 0 )) || return 1

  if [[ $PREVIOUS_THEME_NAME == "$THEME_NAME" ]]; then
    current_background=$(readlink "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ $theme_path != $CURRENT_THEME_PATH && ${current_background%/*} == $current_theme_backgrounds ]]; then
      current_background="$theme_path/backgrounds/${current_background##*/}"
    fi

    index=-1
    for i in "${!backgrounds[@]}"; do
      if [[ ${backgrounds[$i]} == $current_background ]]; then
        index=$i
        break
      fi
    done

    if (( index != -1 )); then
      next_index=$(((index + 1) % ${#backgrounds[@]}))
      CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND="${backgrounds[$next_index]}"
    else
      CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND="${backgrounds[0]}"
    fi
    return
  fi

  state_file=$(theme_background_state_file "$THEME_NAME" 2>/dev/null || true)
  remembered_background=$(cat "$state_file" 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [[ $theme_path != $CURRENT_THEME_PATH && ${remembered_background%/*} == $current_theme_backgrounds ]]; then
    remembered_background="$theme_path/backgrounds/${remembered_background##*/}"
  fi
  if [[ -f $remembered_background ]]; then
    CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND="$remembered_background"
    return
  fi

  CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND="${backgrounds[0]}"
}

choose_staged_theme_background() {
  local next_theme_backgrounds="$NEXT_THEME_PATH/backgrounds"

  choose_theme_background "$NEXT_THEME_PATH" || return 1
  STAGED_THEME_BACKGROUND="$CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND"

  if [[ ${CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND%/*} == $next_theme_backgrounds ]]; then
    CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND="$CURRENT_THEME_PATH/backgrounds/${CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND##*/}"
  fi
}

set_theme_background_link() {
  choose_theme_background || return 1
  ln -nsf "$CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND" "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK"
}

set_theme_background() {
  local new_background new_background_snapshot theme_id intro_prepared=false

  if [[ -z $CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND || ! -f $CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND ]]; then
    if ! choose_theme_background; then
      omarchy-notification-send "$(omarchy-i18n theme.noBackground)" -t 2000
      shell_ipc shell applyTheme "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || true
      return
    fi
  fi

  new_background="$CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND"
  if [[ -n $THEME_BACKGROUND_INTRO ]]; then
    if [[ -n $INTRO_PREPARE_PID ]] && wait "$INTRO_PREPARE_PID"; then
      intro_prepared=true
    fi
    theme_id=$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH")
    THEME_INTRO_TOKEN="$theme_id"
    shell_ipc shell prepareThemeIntro "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT" "$theme_id" "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || \
      shell_ipc shell applyTheme "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || true
    ln -nsf "$new_background" "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK"
    (
      # Played or not, the shell gets the new still: it still holds the old
      # theme's path, which the theme swap above deleted, and loads it again
      # when OWE hands the desktop back after the intro. While the intro plays
      # the shell's background is suspended under it, so the swap is unseen.
      omarchy-theme-bg-boot-intro --theme-switch "$new_background" "$theme_id" "$intro_prepared" || true
      if [[ $(readlink -f "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK") == "$(readlink -f "$new_background")" &&
        $(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH" 2>/dev/null) == "$theme_id" ]]; then
        shell_ipc background setInstant "$new_background" || true
      fi
      shell_ipc shell finishThemeIntro "$theme_id" || true
      wait_for_theme_intro themeIntroStatus "$theme_id" "pending"
      # Reloading Hyprland interrupts video presentation. Wait for playback,
      # then serialize with theme selection so an old intro cannot reload
      # the compositor during the next theme's video.
      (
        flock 9
        if [[ $(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH" 2>/dev/null) == "$theme_id" ]]; then
          omarchy-restart-hyprctl
        fi
      ) 9>"$THEME_SET_LOCK"
      [[ -z $OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT ]] || rm -f "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT"
    ) 9>&- &
    return
  fi
  new_background_snapshot=""
  if [[ -n $PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT && $PREPARED_BACKGROUND == "$new_background" ]]; then
    new_background_snapshot="$PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT"
  else
    [[ -z $PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT ]] || rm -f "$PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT"
    if [[ $BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_SNAPSHOTS == "true" ]]; then
      new_background_snapshot=$(snapshot_background_path "$new_background" "next")
    fi
  fi

  if [[ -f $OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT && -f $new_background_snapshot ]]; then
    shell_ipc background themeTransition "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT" "$new_background_snapshot" "$new_background" "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || \
      shell_ipc shell applyTheme "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || true
    (sleep 3; rm -f "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT" "$new_background_snapshot") &
  elif [[ -f $new_background_snapshot ]]; then
    shell_ipc background themeTransition "" "$new_background_snapshot" "$new_background" "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || \
      shell_ipc shell applyTheme "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || true
    (sleep 3; rm -f "$new_background_snapshot") &
  else
    shell_ipc background themeTransition "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT" "$new_background" "$new_background" "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || \
      shell_ipc shell applyTheme "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || true
    if [[ -f $OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT ]]; then
      (sleep 3; rm -f "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT") &
    fi
  fi

  ln -nsf "$new_background" "$CURRENT_BACKGROUND_LINK"
}

is_denied_installed_file() {
  local name="$1"
  local denied

  [[ $name == *.lua ]] && return 0

  for denied in "${INSTALLED_THEME_DENIED[@]}"; do
    [[ $name == "$denied" ]] && return 0
  done

  return 1
}

# Themes older than colors.toml still get their palette, but their
# alacritty.toml never reaches the staged theme: an Alacritty config names the
# program the terminal launches.
stage_installed_colors_from_alacritty() {
  local source="$1"
  local scratch

  if [[ -f $NEXT_THEME_PATH/colors.toml ]]; then
    return
  fi

  if [[ ! -f $source/alacritty.toml || -L $source/alacritty.toml ]]; then
    return
  fi

  scratch=$(mktemp -d)
  cp "$source/alacritty.toml" "$scratch/alacritty.toml"
  omarchy-theme-colors-from-alacritty "$scratch"

  if [[ -f $scratch/colors.toml ]]; then
    cp "$scratch/colors.toml" "$NEXT_THEME_PATH/colors.toml"
  fi

  rm -rf "$scratch"
}

# Copies a directory without ever following a symlink: in an installed theme one
# points wherever the theme author chose, which is how an unlock.png becomes a
# copy of any file the session can read.
stage_installed_dir() {
  local source="$1"
  local dest="$2"
  local entry name

  mkdir -p "$dest"

  for entry in "$source"/*; do
    [[ -e $entry && ! -L $entry ]] || continue
    name=${entry##*/}

    if [[ -d $entry ]]; then
      stage_installed_dir "$entry" "$dest/$name"
    else
      cp "$entry" "$dest/$name"
    fi
  done
}

# `omarchy theme install` clones into ~/.config/omarchy/themes, so a .git
# directory there means the contents came from a stranger and are held to the
# list above. A directory the user wrote themselves, and a symlink to their own
# working copy, are theirs to fill however they like -- the same distinction
# omarchy-theme-extras draws when it decides which themes it may pull.
theme_came_from_a_repo() {
  local source="$1"

  [[ ! -L $source && -d $source/.git ]]
}

stage_installed_theme() {
  local source="$1"
  local entry name

  [[ -d $source ]] || return 0

  for entry in "$source"/*; do
    [[ -e $entry ]] || continue
    name=${entry##*/}

    if [[ -L $entry ]] || is_denied_installed_file "$name"; then
      case "${name,,}" in
        readme* | license* | changelog* | *.md | *.txt) ;;
        *) IGNORED_THEME_FILES+=("$name") ;;
      esac
    elif [[ -d $entry ]]; then
      stage_installed_dir "$entry" "$NEXT_THEME_PATH/$name"
    else
      cp "$entry" "$NEXT_THEME_PATH/$name"
    fi
  done

  stage_installed_colors_from_alacritty "$source"
}

report_ignored_theme_files() {
  (( ${#IGNORED_THEME_FILES[@]} > 0 )) || return 0

  echo "Ignored in $USER_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME: ${IGNORED_THEME_FILES[*]}" >&2
  echo "A theme installed from a git repo cannot supply Lua, a terminal config, or vscode.json." >&2
}

THEME_NAME=$(echo "$1" | sed -E 's/<[^>]+>//g' | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr ' ' '-')
THEME_HEADLESS=0
if [[ ${OMARCHY_THEME_HEADLESS:-} == "1" || ${OMARCHY_THEME_OFFLINE:-} == "1" ]]; then
  THEME_HEADLESS=1
fi

if [[ -z $THEME_NAME || $THEME_NAME == .* || $THEME_NAME == */* ]]; then
  echo "Invalid theme name: $1"
  exit 1
fi

if [[ ! -d $OMARCHY_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME ]] && [[ ! -d $USER_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME ]]; then
  echo "Theme '$THEME_NAME' does not exist"
  exit 1
fi

# Serialize theme changes. Theme switching rebuilds a shared next-theme staging
# directory and updates current theme/background symlinks; concurrent calls can
# otherwise race and make one selection appear to be ignored.
exec 9>"$THEME_SET_LOCK"
flock 9

# A current video frame only represents the screen after its opening fade.
# Finish that short reveal before capturing the next outgoing cover.
if [[ $THEME_HEADLESS != "1" && $OMARCHY_THEME_SKIP_BACKGROUND != "1" ]]; then
  wait_for_theme_intro themeIntroStatus "$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH" 2>/dev/null)" "pending"
fi

PREVIOUS_THEME_NAME=$(cat "$CURRENT_THEME_NAME_PATH" 2>/dev/null || true)
remember_current_theme_background

# Setup clean next theme directory (for atomic theme config swapping)
rm -rf "$NEXT_THEME_PATH"
mkdir -p "$NEXT_THEME_PATH"

# Copy official theme first, then overlay the user's theme on top
cp -r "$OMARCHY_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME/"* "$NEXT_THEME_PATH/" 2>/dev/null

if theme_came_from_a_repo "$USER_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME"; then
  stage_installed_theme "$USER_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME"
  report_ignored_theme_files
else
  cp -r "$USER_THEMES_PATH/$THEME_NAME/"* "$NEXT_THEME_PATH/" 2>/dev/null
fi

# Generate colors.toml from alacritty.toml if theme is missing colors.toml
if [[ ! -f $NEXT_THEME_PATH/colors.toml && -f $NEXT_THEME_PATH/alacritty.toml ]]; then
  omarchy-theme-colors-from-alacritty "$NEXT_THEME_PATH"
fi

CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND=""
STAGED_THEME_BACKGROUND=""
OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT=""
PREPARED_BACKGROUND=""
PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT=""
BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_SNAPSHOTS=true
THEME_BACKGROUND_INTRO=""
INTRO_PREPARE_PID=""
THEME_INTRO_TOKEN=""
if [[ $THEME_HEADLESS != "1" && $OMARCHY_THEME_SKIP_BACKGROUND != "1" ]]; then
  # Resolve the staged choice while the old theme still exists. Video changes
  # switch directly to the durable path in QML, so neither side needs a copy.
  if choose_staged_theme_background; then
    if [[ $PREVIOUS_THEME_NAME != "$THEME_NAME" && ! -f $HOME/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/background-intros-off ]] &&
      [[ $(hyprctl -j getoption animations:enabled 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.bool') == "true" ]]; then
      THEME_BACKGROUND_INTRO=$(omarchy-theme-bg-boot-intro --resolve-only "$STAGED_THEME_BACKGROUND")
    fi
    if [[ -n $THEME_BACKGROUND_INTRO ]]; then
      OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT=$(snapshot_current_background)
      # OWE retains the opened clip across the staged directory's rename.
      owe intro-prepare "$THEME_BACKGROUND_INTRO" >/dev/null 2>&1 9>&- &
      INTRO_PREPARE_PID=$!
      shell_ipc shell prepareThemeIntro "$OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT" "$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$NEXT_THEME_PATH")" "" "" || true
    elif background_transition_uses_snapshots "$CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND"; then
      OLD_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT=$(snapshot_current_background)

      # Hand the shell the next background now, so it decodes while the
      # templates render and the theme swaps in. The staged file is the same
      # inode the swap moves into place, so its snapshot is the final image.
      PREPARED_BACKGROUND="$CHOSEN_THEME_BACKGROUND"
      PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT=$(snapshot_background_path "$STAGED_THEME_BACKGROUND" "next")
      if [[ -n $PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT ]]; then
        shell_ipc background prepare "$PREPARED_BACKGROUND_SNAPSHOT" 9>&- &
      fi
    else
      BACKGROUND_TRANSITION_SNAPSHOTS=false
    fi
  fi
fi

# Generate dynamic configs
omarchy-theme-set-templates

# Replacing the theme's still can cancel an active OWE intro even before the
# background link changes. Present its cover before replacing either path.
if [[ -n $THEME_BACKGROUND_INTRO ]]; then
  wait_for_theme_intro themeIntroCoverStatus "$(stat -Lc '%d:%i' "$NEXT_THEME_PATH")" "loading"
fi

# Swap next theme in as current
rm -rf "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH"
mv "$NEXT_THEME_PATH" "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH"
# Name this switch, so its deferred retints can tell when a later one replaced
# the theme. A directory's inode would do, except that it can be reused.
# A token that could not be written proves nothing either way, so then the
# retints run as if this switch were the latest.
APPLIED_THEME_GENERATION="$$-${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/}"
if ! printf '%s\n' "$APPLIED_THEME_GENERATION" 2>/dev/null >"$THEME_GENERATION_PATH"; then
  APPLIED_THEME_GENERATION=""
fi

# Store theme name for reference
echo "$THEME_NAME" >"$CURRENT_THEME_NAME_PATH"

# Make the running shell pick up the new palette immediately while the rest of
# the theme hooks run.
colors_payload=$([[ -f $CURRENT_THEME_PATH/colors.toml ]] && base64 -w 0 "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH/colors.toml")
shell_payload=$([[ -f $CURRENT_THEME_PATH/shell.toml ]] && base64 -w 0 "$CURRENT_THEME_PATH/shell.toml")
if [[ $THEME_HEADLESS == "1" ]]; then
  # No shell/session bus exists during ISO chroot finalization, but the first
  # real login still needs a current background symlink for omarchy-shell to
  # render.
  [[ $OMARCHY_THEME_SKIP_BACKGROUND == "1" ]] || set_theme_background_link || true
elif [[ $OMARCHY_THEME_SKIP_BACKGROUND == "1" ]]; then
  shell_ipc shell applyTheme "$colors_payload" "$shell_payload" || true
else
  set_theme_background
fi

# The shared staging/current symlinks are updated and the shell has accepted
# the transition. Let another theme selection queue only behind that critical
# section, not behind slower app-retint hooks and selector cache warmups.
flock -u 9

# What the user is looking at: the terminals and the programs drawn inside
# them, plus the window borders when no intro is playing. These run as soon as
# the theme is in place, alongside the wallpaper and bar transition.
visible_theme_commands=(
  omarchy-restart-terminal
  omarchy-theme-set-foot
  omarchy-theme-set-tmux
  omarchy-restart-btop
  omarchy-restart-opencode
  omarchy-restart-helix
  omarchy-theme-set-hunk
)

# Configs other apps read on their next refresh or launch: GTK, the browser
# policy, editors, agents and the keyboard backlight. Nothing on screen waits
# for these.
other_theme_commands=(
  omarchy-theme-set-gnome
  omarchy-theme-set-pi
  omarchy-theme-set-claude
  omarchy-theme-set-hermes
  omarchy-theme-set-t3code
  omarchy-theme-set-browser
  omarchy-theme-set-vscode
  omarchy-theme-set-obsidian
  omarchy-theme-set-keyboard
  omarchy-theme-set-fcitx5
)

theme_still_current() {
  [[ -z $APPLIED_THEME_GENERATION ]] && return 0
  [[ $(<"$THEME_GENERATION_PATH") == "$APPLIED_THEME_GENERATION" ]] 2>/dev/null
}

apply_other_theme_commands() {
  local detached="${1:-}"

  # Let an intro's wallpaper and bar finish their reveal before these compete
  # with video decoding and the shell's frame rendering.
  if [[ -n $THEME_INTRO_TOKEN ]]; then
    wait_for_theme_intro themeIntroStatus "$THEME_INTRO_TOKEN" "pending"
  fi

  # Warm the background selector's thumbnails, which converts images on every
  # core, so it too waits for the reveal. The theme picker keeps its own rows
  # in the shell and refreshes them each time it opens.
  omarchy-theme-bg-cache </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 8>&- 9>&- &

  # Quick switches leave several of these batches going, and a retint such as
  # the browser's reads its colour long before it writes it. Run the batches
  # one at a time, and skip the retints of one whose theme was replaced while
  # it waited, so an older theme never lands after a newer one.
  exec 8>"$THEME_RETINT_LOCK"
  flock 8
  local current=false
  if theme_still_current; then
    current=true
  fi

  # The log starts over with each batch that retints, and a superseded one
  # leaves it to the newer batch. An older batch's hook may still be writing to
  # it, so every batch appends rather than writing at its own offset.
  if [[ $detached == "detached" ]]; then
    if [[ $current == "true" ]]; then
      : >"$THEME_SET_LOG"
    fi
    exec 2>>"$THEME_SET_LOG"
  fi
  if [[ $current == "true" ]]; then
    run_parallel "${other_theme_commands[@]}"
  fi
  exec 8>&-

  # Call hook on theme set. The lock is released first: a hook may switch the
  # theme itself, and that switch's batch needs the lock.
  omarchy-hook theme-set "$THEME_NAME" >/dev/null

  # A newer switch replaced this theme during the hook, so its failures say
  # nothing about the apps any more; the newer batch reports its own.
  if theme_still_current; then
    report_failed_theme_commands "$detached"
  fi
}

if [[ $THEME_HEADLESS != "1" ]]; then
  # An intro reloads Hyprland after playback; ordinary theme changes reload it
  # with the terminals.
  if [[ -z $THEME_INTRO_TOKEN ]]; then
    visible_theme_commands+=(omarchy-restart-hyprctl)
  fi
  run_parallel "${visible_theme_commands[@]}"

  # A switch from the theme picker, the menu or a script returns once what is
  # on screen has changed and leaves the rest running behind it, with its
  # output in the log. One typed in a terminal waits for everything, so the
  # browser policy can ask for a sudo password there, and so does a caller
  # that sets OMARCHY_THEME_WAIT=1 because it reads those app configs next.
  if [[ -t 0 || ${OMARCHY_THEME_WAIT:-} == "1" ]]; then
    apply_other_theme_commands
  else
    mkdir -p "${THEME_SET_LOG%/*}"
    apply_other_theme_commands detached </dev/null >/dev/null 2>/dev/null 9>&- &
  fi

  # Mirror the theme to herdr machines. SSH can take a while, so this never holds up the theme change.
  setsid omarchy-theme-set-herdr-machines >>"$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/theme-set-herdr-machines.log" 2>&1 </dev/null &
fi

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-browser
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Apply the current theme color to Chromium, Chrome, Edge, and Brave
# omarchy:hidden=true

source "$OMARCHY_PATH/install/helpers/browser-policy.sh"

CHROMIUM_THEME=$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/chromium.theme
THEME_HEX_COLOR=$BROWSER_POLICY_DEFAULT_COLOR

if [[ -f $CHROMIUM_THEME ]]; then
  THEME_HEX_COLOR=$(browser_policy_theme_hex "$(<$CHROMIUM_THEME)")
fi

# Tests override this with a temporary directory list; production uses the
# fixed trust-root set from browser-policy.sh.
POLICY_DIRS=("${BROWSER_POLICY_MANAGED_DIRS[@]}")
if [[ -n ${OMARCHY_BROWSER_POLICY_DIRS:-} ]]; then
  POLICY_DIRS=()
  while IFS= read -r dir; do
    POLICY_DIRS+=("$dir")
  done <<< "$OMARCHY_BROWSER_POLICY_DIRS"
fi

# A managed color.json is already correct only when it is a regular, root-owned
# file with mode 0644 containing exactly the canonical JSON for the requested
# color.
file_is_canonical() {
  local file=$1
  [[ -f $file && ! -L $file ]] || return 1
  [[ $(<"$file") == "$expected_json" ]] || return 1
  [[ $(stat -c '%U:%G %a' "$file") == "root:root 644" ]]
}

# Skip the privileged policy write and browser refreshes entirely when every
# existing managed color.json is already canonical. The writer only touches
# directories that exist, so a browser installed since then has no color.json
# yet and takes the write.
expected_json='{"BrowserThemeColor": "'$THEME_HEX_COLOR'", "BrowserColorScheme": "device"}'
saw_any=false
all_unchanged=true
for dir in "${POLICY_DIRS[@]}"; do
  [[ -d $dir && ! -L $dir ]] || continue
  saw_any=true

  if ! file_is_canonical "$dir/color.json"; then
    all_unchanged=false
    break
  fi
done
$saw_any && $all_unchanged && exit 0

failed=0
# A script's background job reads /dev/null unless told otherwise, which would
# turn the writer's terminal sudo prompt into a pkexec dialog. Keep stdin.
omarchy-theme-set-browser-policy "${THEME_HEX_COLOR#\#}" <&0 &
policy_pid=$!

# While the policy writes, find the running browsers with one process table
# read. A pgrep per browser rescans /proc each time, ~40ms apiece.
declare -A running_names=()
running_args=""
while read -r name args; do
  running_names[$name]=1
  running_args+="$args"$'\n'
done < <(ps -eo comm=,args=)

# Chrome installs as either binary name, so take whichever exists.
chrome=google-chrome-stable
omarchy-cmd-present "$chrome" || chrome=google-chrome

browsers_to_refresh=()
for browser in chromium:chromium "chrome:$chrome" msedge:microsoft-edge-stable brave:brave; do
  [[ -n ${running_names[${browser%%:*}]:-} ]] && omarchy-cmd-present "${browser#*:}" && browsers_to_refresh+=("${browser#*:}")
done
# Match on the binary path: the running process is named plain "brave", and a
# bare brave-origin pattern would also match the installer's own terminal.
[[ $running_args == *"/opt/brave-origin-bin/"* ]] && omarchy-cmd-present brave-origin && browsers_to_refresh+=(brave-origin)

wait "$policy_pid" || failed=1

# Refresh each running browser in parallel, so one slow launch doesn't
# serialize the rest.
refresh_pids=()
for command in "${browsers_to_refresh[@]}"; do
  "$command" --refresh-platform-policy --no-startup-window &>/dev/null &
  refresh_pids+=("$!")
done

for pid in "${refresh_pids[@]}"; do
  wait "$pid"
done

exit "$failed"

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-claude
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Sync the generated Omarchy theme to Claude Code
# omarchy:args=[--activate]
# omarchy:hidden=true

set -euo pipefail

CLAUDE_SOURCE_PATH="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/claude.json"
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}"
CLAUDE_THEME_PATH="$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/themes/omarchy.json"
CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH="$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/settings.json"
CLAUDE_ACTIVATE=0

usage() {
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-set-claude [--activate]"
}

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --activate)
      CLAUDE_ACTIVATE=1
      ;;
    -h | --help)
      usage
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

if [[ ! -f $CLAUDE_SOURCE_PATH ]]; then
  if (( CLAUDE_ACTIVATE == 1 )); then
    echo "Claude Code theme source missing: $CLAUDE_SOURCE_PATH" >&2
    echo "Run omarchy-theme-refresh after selecting an Omarchy theme." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  exit 0
fi

if (( CLAUDE_ACTIVATE == 0 )) && [[ ! -d $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

write_setting_theme() {
  local tmp

  if [[ -f $CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH ]]; then
    tmp=$(mktemp "$CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH.XXXXXX")
    jq '.theme = "custom:omarchy"' "$CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH" >"$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH"
  else
    cat >"$CLAUDE_SETTINGS_PATH" <<EOF
{
  "theme": "custom:omarchy"
}
EOF
  fi
}

# Claude Code watches ~/.claude/themes and hot-reloads the file on change,
# so running sessions retint without a restart.
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$CLAUDE_THEME_PATH")"
tmp=$(mktemp "$CLAUDE_THEME_PATH.XXXXXX")
cp "$CLAUDE_SOURCE_PATH" "$tmp"
mv "$tmp" "$CLAUDE_THEME_PATH"

if (( CLAUDE_ACTIVATE == 1 )); then
  write_setting_theme
fi

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-fcitx5
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Sync the generated Omarchy theme to the Fcitx candidate window
# omarchy:args=[--activate]
# omarchy:hidden=true

set -euo pipefail

THEME_SOURCE="$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/fcitx5-theme.conf"
THEME_DIR="${XDG_DATA_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share}/fcitx5/themes/omarchy"
CLASSICUI_CONF="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/fcitx5/conf/classicui.conf"
PACKAGED_THEME="${OMARCHY_FCITX5_PACKAGED_THEME:-/usr/share/fcitx5/themes/default}"
ACTIVATE=0

usage() {
  echo "Usage: omarchy-theme-set-fcitx5 [--activate]"
}

for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --activate)
      ACTIVATE=1
      ;;
    -h | --help)
      usage
      exit 0
      ;;
    *)
      usage >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

# Point classicui at the theme, unless the user picked one of their own. A
# configtool save writes Theme=default even when only the font changed, so the
# stock themes count as unpicked. Only activation does this, so a later choice
# of fcitx5's own theme sticks.
select_theme() {
  local conf original updated key value

  conf=$(realpath -m "$CLASSICUI_CONF")
  original=$([[ -f $conf ]] && cat "$conf" || true)
  updated=$original

  for key in Theme DarkTheme; do
    value=$(sed -n "s/^$key=//p" <<<"$updated" | tail -n 1)
    if [[ -z $value ]]; then
      updated+="${updated:+$'\n'}$key=omarchy"
    elif [[ $value == "default" || $value == "default-dark" ]]; then
      updated=$(sed "s/^$key=.*/$key=omarchy/" <<<"$updated")
    fi
  done

  if [[ $updated != "$original" ]]; then
    # Write through a dotfiles symlink rather than replacing it.
    mkdir -p "${conf%/*}"
    printf '%s\n' "$updated" >"$conf.omarchy-tmp"
    mv "$conf.omarchy-tmp" "$conf"
  fi
}

# Until activation there is no theme directory, and nothing to keep in step.
if (( ACTIVATE == 0 )) && [[ ! -d $THEME_DIR ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$THEME_DIR"
if [[ -f $THEME_SOURCE ]]; then
  tmp=$(mktemp "$THEME_DIR/theme.conf.XXXXXX")
  cp "$THEME_SOURCE" "$tmp"
  mv "$tmp" "$THEME_DIR/theme.conf"
fi

# Image= entries resolve inside the theme's own directory. fcitx5's page and
# menu glyphs are neutral grey, so the packaged ones suit every palette.
for glyph in "$PACKAGED_THEME"/*.svg; do
  [[ -e $glyph ]] && ln -sfn "$glyph" "$THEME_DIR/${glyph##*/}"
done

if (( ACTIVATE == 1 )); then
  select_theme
fi

# classicui reads its theme only when its config loads. Never start Fcitx just
# to tell it.
busctl --user --auto-start=no call org.fcitx.Fcitx5 /controller org.fcitx.Fcitx.Controller1 \
  ReloadAddonConfig s classicui >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-foot
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Apply current Omarchy theme colors and background alpha to running Foot terminals
# omarchy:hidden=true

colors_toml=$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/colors.toml
foot_ini=$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/foot.ini

[[ -f $colors_toml ]] || exit 0

# Theme switches wait on this retint, and pgrep scans every process, so it runs
# once; each terminal's shells come from the kernel's list of its children.
foot_pids=$(pgrep -x foot) || exit 0

foot_osc=$(omarchy-theme-osc "$colors_toml")
[[ -n $foot_osc ]] || exit 0

# foot takes a background alpha as an urxvt-style [percent] prefix, so a theme
# going see-through or back, as with Glassy windows, reaches running terminals.
# The last alpha in the theme's foot.ini wins, as it does when foot reads it.
alpha=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*alpha[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*\([0-9.]*\).*/\1/p' "$foot_ini" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
background=$(omarchy-theme-color --file "$colors_toml" background 2>/dev/null)
if [[ -n $background ]]; then
  percent=$(awk -v alpha="${alpha:-1}" 'BEGIN { printf "%d", alpha * 100 + 0.5 }')
  foot_osc+=$(printf '\033]11;[%d]%s\007' "$percent" "$background")
fi

for foot_pid in $foot_pids; do
  children="/proc/$foot_pid/task/$foot_pid/children"
  if [[ -e $children ]]; then
    { child_pids=$(<"$children"); } 2>/dev/null || continue
  else
    # A kernel built without CONFIG_PROC_CHILDREN keeps no such list.
    child_pids=$(pgrep -P "$foot_pid")
  fi
  for child_pid in $child_pids; do
    tty=$(readlink "/proc/$child_pid/fd/1" 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ $tty == /dev/pts/* ]]; then
      printf '%b' "$foot_osc" >"$tty"
    fi
  done
done

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-glass
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Give terminals, btop, and GTK apps a see-through background while windows are glassy
# omarchy:args=[theme-dir]
# omarchy:hidden=true

# A Hyprland opacity rule fades a terminal's text along with its background,
# and foot turns compositor blur down unless its own config asks for it, so the
# glass belongs in each terminal's theme file, as in the glassy Starship
# (#14726). The lines sit between markers so leaving glassy takes them out
# again, and a theme that sets its own opacity keeps it.

THEME_DIR="${1:-$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme}"
TOGGLES_DIR="${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/omarchy/toggles/hypr"
GLASSY=false
[[ -f $TOGGLES_DIR/window-glassy.lua ]] && GLASSY=true
status=0

# A literal for a sed address, whose delimiter is /.
regex() {
  sed 's/[][\\.*^$/]/\\&/g' <<<"$1"
}

# A block added to a file that did not end in a newline has to supply one, so
# its begin marker says so, and taking the block out takes that newline back.
# Leaving glassy then gives the file back exactly as it was. Markers come as
# an opening and a closing part, so CSS can wrap them in a comment.
remove_block() {
  local file="$1" open="$2" close="$3"
  local begin end
  # Theme switches wait on this, and a freshly rendered file has no block, so
  # look for one before building its sed addresses.
  [[ -f $file ]] && grep -qF "$open omarchy-glass begin" "$file" || return 0
  begin=$(regex "$open omarchy-glass begin")
  end=$(regex "$open omarchy-glass end$close")

  local added_newline=false
  grep -qxF "$open omarchy-glass begin after a line without a newline$close" "$file" && added_newline=true
  sed -i "/^$begin/,/^$end\$/d" "$file" || return 1
  if [[ $added_newline == "true" && -s $file && -z $(tail -c 1 "$file") ]]; then
    truncate -s -1 "$file" || return 1
  fi
}

append_block() {
  local file="$1" open="$2" close="$3" lines="$4"
  if [[ -s $file && -n $(tail -c 1 "$file") ]]; then
    printf '\n%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$open omarchy-glass begin after a line without a newline$close" "$lines" "$open omarchy-glass end$close" >>"$file"
  else
    printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$open omarchy-glass begin$close" "$lines" "$open omarchy-glass end$close" >>"$file"
  fi
}

# Each setting comes with a pattern for the theme setting it already, which
# keeps the theme's own; an empty pattern always adds it. Lines that belong in
# a section go in under its header. A file that already has the section gets
# them inside it, since TOML refuses a table declared twice; otherwise the
# header comes along with them.
glass() {
  local file="$THEME_DIR/$1" section="$2"
  shift 2
  [[ -f $file ]] || return 0

  remove_block "$file" "#" "" || return 1
  [[ $GLASSY == "true" ]] || return 0

  local lines=""
  while (( $# >= 2 )); do
    if [[ -z $1 ]] || ! grep -qE "$1" "$file"; then
      lines+="${lines:+$'\n'}$2"
    fi
    shift 2
  done
  [[ -n $lines ]] || return 0

  # A header may carry trailing space or a comment.
  local header="^$(regex "$section")[[:space:]]*(#.*)?\$"
  if [[ -n $section ]] && grep -qE "$header" "$file"; then
    local block
    block=$(mktemp) || return 1
    printf '# omarchy-glass begin\n%s\n# omarchy-glass end\n' "$lines" >"$block"
    sed -i -E "0,/$header/{/$header/r $block
}" "$file"
    local result=$?
    rm -f "$block"
    return $result
  fi

  append_block "$file" "#" "" "${section:+$section$'\n'}$lines"
}

# Alacritty's own blur works only on macOS and KDE; Hyprland blurs it anyway.
glass alacritty.toml '[window]' \
  '^[[:space:]]*opacity[[:space:]]*=' 'opacity = 0.65' || status=1
glass foot.ini '[colors-dark]' \
  '^[[:space:]]*alpha[[:space:]]*=' 'alpha=0.65' \
  '^[[:space:]]*blur[[:space:]]*=' 'blur=yes' || status=1
glass kitty.conf '' \
  '^[[:space:]]*background_opacity[[:space:]]' 'background_opacity 0.65' || status=1
# btop paints its own background over the terminal's glass. An empty main_bg
# uses the terminal background; the last theme value wins, so removing the
# block restores the theme's colour without changing btop's user config.
glass btop.theme '' \
  '^[[:space:]]*theme\[main_bg\][[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*""' 'theme[main_bg]=""' || status=1
# GTK only asks Hyprland for blur under a CSS backdrop-filter, which Ghostty
# takes as custom CSS and reloads live; its background-blur speaks only KDE's
# blur protocol.
glass ghostty.conf '' \
  '^[[:space:]]*background-opacity[[:space:]]*=' 'background-opacity = 0.65' \
  '' "gtk-custom-css = $OMARCHY_PATH/default/gtk/glass.css" || status=1

# Other GTK apps, such as Nautilus, read the user's gtk.css at launch, so the
# same backdrop blur is imported there. It follows the mode alone, so a theme
# switch, which names the theme it is rendering, leaves it be.
if (( $# == 0 )); then
  gtk_css="${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/gtk-4.0/gtk.css"
  remove_block "$gtk_css" "/*" " */" || status=1
  if [[ $GLASSY == "true" ]]; then
    { mkdir -p "${gtk_css%/*}" &&
      append_block "$gtk_css" "/*" " */" "@import url(\"file://$OMARCHY_PATH/default/gtk/glass.css\");"; } || status=1
  fi
fi

exit $status

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-gnome
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Apply the current theme to GNOME color mode and icon settings
# omarchy:hidden=true

# gsettings needs a user DBus session. During ISO installs this command can be
# reached from arch-chroot while applying the initial Omarchy theme; defer until
# the user has a real session instead of emitting dconf warnings.
if [[ -z ${DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS:-} ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

THEME_DIR=$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme
COLORS_FILE="$THEME_DIR/colors.toml"

# omarchy-theme-color resolves mode from colors.toml (`mode = "light"`), a
# legacy light.mode marker beside it, or background luminance for user themes.
mode=$(omarchy-theme-color --file "$COLORS_FILE" mode)

if [[ $mode == "light" ]]; then
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme "prefer-light"
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme "Adwaita"
else
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme "prefer-dark"
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme "Adwaita-dark"
fi

# Change gnome icon theme color
GNOME_ICONS_THEME=$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/icons.theme
if [[ -f $GNOME_ICONS_THEME ]]; then
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface icon-theme "$(<$GNOME_ICONS_THEME)"
else
  gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface icon-theme "Yaru-blue"
fi

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-herdr-machines
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Mirror the current theme to your herdr machines that run Omarchy
# omarchy:args=[--available]
# omarchy:hidden=true

# omarchy-theme-set runs this in the background after every theme change. Sync is off until
# the herdr-theme-sync toggle is turned on, and a machine only accepts themes with it on too.

# Columns: id, label, SSH target, session, state.
# This machine may be listed too, and it is already on the theme, so it needs no special case.
targets=$(herdr machine list 2>/dev/null | awk -F '\t' '$5 == "enabled" { print $3 }')

# The menu offers the toggle whenever there is a machine to sync to, whether or not sync is on.
if [[ $1 == "--available" ]]; then
  [[ -n $targets ]]
  exit
fi

# Serialize runs and send whichever theme is current once the lock is held,
# so a slow earlier run can never overwrite a later theme change.
exec 9>"${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/omarchy-theme-set-herdr-machines.lock"
flock 9

# A theme that arrived from another machine stops here, so machines never echo it back.
# The toggle is checked once the lock is held, so turning sync off also stops a queued run.
if [[ -n $OMARCHY_THEME_SYNC_FROM ]] || ! omarchy-toggle-enabled herdr-theme-sync; then
  exit 0
fi

theme=$(cat "$HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.name" 2>/dev/null)
control_dir="$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-theme-sync"
mkdir -m 700 -p "$control_dir"

# Runs on the remote machine under a login shell, so OMARCHY_PATH and PATH are set there.
# SSH carries no desktop session, so the environment comes from the live Hyprland instance.
# The flag is read directly, so an Omarchy that predates theme sync simply counts as off.
# Braces make bash read the whole script before running it, so nothing it runs can consume the rest.
read -r -d '' REMOTE_SCRIPT <<'EOF'
{
  if [[ ! -f ~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/herdr-theme-sync ]]; then
    echo "theme sync is off"
    exit
  fi

  if [[ $(cat ~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.name 2>/dev/null) == "$theme" ]]; then
    echo "already on $theme"
    exit
  fi

  export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="/run/user/$(id -u)"
  instance=$(hyprctl instances -j 2>/dev/null | jq -r 'max_by(.time) // empty | "\(.instance) \(.wl_socket)"')
  if [[ -z $instance ]]; then
    echo "no Hyprland session"
    exit
  fi

  read -r HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE WAYLAND_DISPLAY <<<"$instance"
  export HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE WAYLAND_DISPLAY
  export DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS="unix:path=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus"
  export OMARCHY_THEME_SYNC_FROM="$from"

  if omarchy theme set "$theme" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "set $theme"
  else
    echo "failed to set $theme"
  fi
} </dev/null
EOF

# Reuse each authenticated connection for ten idle minutes, so an SSH agent like
# 1Password does not need to approve every theme change. Connect one machine at a time.
# SSH joins its arguments into a shell command, so the theme travels on stdin as a quoted assignment.
for target in $targets; do
  result=$(printf 'theme=%q from=%q\n%s\n' "$theme" "$(hostname)" "$REMOTE_SCRIPT" |
    timeout 60 ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 \
      -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=600 -o "ControlPath=$control_dir/%C" \
      "$target" bash -l -s 2>&1 | tail -n 1)
  echo "$(date '+%F %T') $target: ${result:-unreachable}"
done

### omarchy/bin/omarchy-theme-set-hunk
#!/bin/bash

# omarchy:summary=Tell running Hunk sessions to pick up the new terminal colors
# omarchy:hidden=true

# Hunk's default terminal theme re-reads the terminal palette on SIGWINCH. Terminals reload
# their colors in parallel with this hook, so nudge once now and once after they have settled;
# Hunk only repaints when the palette actually changed. The second nudge waits in the
# background: omarchy-theme-set holds its theme-set hook until every retint returns.

if pgrep -x hunk >/dev/null; then
  pkill -WINCH -x hunk
  (sleep 1; pkill -WINCH -x hunk) >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
fi
